assumptions: Task tree branching factor serves as a valid proxy for structural complexity.
Decentralized agent coordination can be simulated through iterative task decomposition.
Convergence can be identified within defined simulation bounds.
definition.falsification: The mean branching factor remains statistically indistinguishable from a random null model.
definition.statement: Intelligent decentralized agents operating on varied task distributions without explicit central coordination will converge toward measurable structural complexity, as evidenced by increasing branching factors in task trees.
definition.uncertainty: The definition of 'complexity' in unprompted agent task trees is highly sensitive to the initial task distribution parameters.

definition.method: Simulate decentralized agent task decomposition using a synthetic tree-growth model where agents select tasks from a distribution without global oversight.
definition.stop: Completion of 200 iterations or error state.
definition.success: Measured branching factor consistently exceeds 1.5 with p < 0.05.
